obligation: G107 -- RPT and RPS measured on the LIVE runtime alongside TPS
RPT_is_reported_live_and_correctly_does_: RPT is 130 in all three runs. That is not the instrument failing to respond -- it is the instrument being RIGHT. A route is a semantic state transition (G106), and none of these toggles removes one: they swap kernels inside routes. An RPT that moved when a kernel was swapped would be counting dispatches, which is precisely the confusion G106 exists to prevent.
RPS_does_move_because_TPS_does: RPS spans 4263 to 4272 routes/second across the three runs, tracking measured TPS. RPS is live because TPS is live; RPT is structural. Reporting both is what separates 'the program got faster' from 'the program got simpler'.

the_verify_half_that_could_NOT_be_demons.asked: run before/after a known fusion, show RPT change
the_verify_half_that_could_NOT_be_demons.why_not: No toggle in this runtime removes a ROUTE. HAWKING_QWEN38_RECON_FUSE=0 selects different kernel family NAMES at a constant 964 dispatches -- verified, 964 in both states -- so it is a kernel swap, not a fusion. Merging block halves is what would move RPT and nothing does that.
the_verify_half_that_could_NOT_be_demons.missing_input: a route-level fusion, i.e. one that merges a mixer and an MLP into a single schedulable transition

an_anomaly_named_rather_than_resolved: HAWKING_ARGMAX_TWO_PASS=1 is a LIVE knob -- its env parsing was read and is correct -- and the two-pass path dispatches two kernels where one-pass dispatches one. The reported dispatch count is 964 in BOTH states. So either the counter's scope excludes the sampling dispatch, or the two-pass path is not being taken. This is recorded as an open question rather than resolved, because guessing which would put an unverified claim in the ledger.
